newsitem.title: USA: Flinn said "unlikely" to get honorable discharge.
newsitem.headline: Flinn said "unlikely" to get honorable discharge.

text.p: Air Force Secretary Sheila Widnall is "very, very unlikely" to grant female bomber pilot Kelly Flinn an honourable discharge to avoid court-martial on charges of adultery, a senior Air Force offical said Monday.
"It is going to be very, very unlikely that the secretary will allow an honourable discharge," the official told Reuters when asked if Flinn's request for the step would be granted.

First Lieutenant Flinn is scheduled to go on trial at Minot Air Force Base in North Dakota Tuesday. The Air Force's first female B-52 pilot is seeking to resign with an honourable discharge to avoid court martial on charges of adultery and fraternisation.

The official, who asked not to be named, said that the Air Force Judge Advocate General's office at the Pentagon was likely to grant a delay in the court martial Tuesday morning, pending a decision by Widnall on the request from Flinn.

The senior Air Force official said the request from Flinn's lawyers for her to be allowed to resign under honourable circumstances was expected to reach Widnall through the Air Force chain of command within days.
"But the precedent in this case makes it extremely unlikely that she would grant the request," the official added.

Other Air Force officials said that the charges were much more serious than adultery, because they involved fraternisation with a lower-ranking Air Force enlisted man, as well as lying and disobeying an order.
Flinn, 26 and single, has acknowledged having had an affair with a married civilian and is also accused of having sex with a lower-ranking enlisted man. She is also accused of lying.

Conviction of adultery in a military trial is punishable by penalties ranging up to dishonourable discharge and possible fines and imprisonment. Critics have argued that Flinn's case highlights a double standard in the way the U.S. Armed Forces treats the issue of adultery among its male and female staff.
